name: A Run Applies ESOI
description: A deep run follows the specification of what it works on, and leaves its metric result before and after.
purpose: A deep run applies ESOI behaviour: it carries the method in its standing instructions, is shown the slice of the specification its goal serves before the task, and has its metric read before and after and written to the run's record.
approach: Carry the ESOI method in the deep run's standing instructions, put the slice of the specification the goal serves (its next milestone and the metric that measures it) into the brief, and have the runner read that metric before and after the work and write both readings to the run's record.
out_of_scope: Editing ESOI records (adding or changing a record or field), and the mechanics of reading a metric's value or drafting a metric for a task that has none.
milestones: 1. Every deep run's metric result before and after is recorded by code (selected by direction, 2026-10-21). 2. Replayed tasks are accepted on the first attempt at least as often as without the slice (task_replay).
measures_of_success: Replayed tasks pass the done verifier on the first attempt, runs that change something leave a durable attributed record of the before and after reading, and the principles in the instructions are followed in replies. Standing conditions: a repository without records or a goal with no working folder gets no slice and the run waits for nothing.
parameters: The arm, the meters that read a metric (QAR_METRIC_METERS), and the bound on a reading.
inputs: The goal text and the working folder of the run.
outputs: A slice of the specification for the brief, or none, and the before and after readings.
effects: Runs the meters around a deep goal and appends the readings to the metric ledger; no model call of its own.
usage_notes: Distinct from esoi-application (the hub's job: apply a proposed edit to ESOI records), from metric-translation (turns a request into a metric with a target and reads it) and from goal-completion (judges whether a decision or goal is done): this one is only how a run behaves around its own goal. A lane turns the code's part off with ESOI_SELECT_QUEST_AI_RUNNER_ITERATE_BY_SPEC=generic-doctrine.
